title: Oncogene-induced cancer can be detected early by bioelectrical imaging

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Oncogene-induced cancer can be detected early by bioelectrical imaging

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Cancer induced in vivo by human oncogenes can be detected early by bioelectrical (membrane-voltage) imaging, as predicted by the view of cancer as a failure of bioelectric 'cognitive glue'.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Cancer and the Scaling of the Self

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It has now been shown that (a) cancer induced by human oncogenes in vivo can be detected early by bioelectrical imaging [175]

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine”, BioEssays : news and reviews in molecular, cellular and developmental biology (2025), doi:10.1002/bies.202400196; section “Cancer and the Scaling of the Self”. Scope: Xenopus laevis embryos expressing human oncogenes (author's lab's prior work, ref [175])

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2025-wisdom-15: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.69

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Early detection is a direct classification problem with a clear temporal endpoint. Published measurements can support the reported model, but independent analysis depends on access to raw pre-phenotype voltage images and animal-level outcomes.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Blindly classify oncogene-expressing Xenopus embryos from membrane-voltage images acquired before visible tumours and compare predictions with later tumour status and uninjected controls. Above-chance early discrimination with calibrated specificity supports the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The decisive raw image series may not be deposited.

Image analysis must be blinded to oncogene-expression markers.

Detection in Xenopus does not establish clinical sensitivity.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.95
analysis feasibility: 0.75
data existence: 0.45
discriminating power: 0.85
data adequacy: 0.5

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Early detection by voltage imaging is a defined classification problem with a time order. The Xenopus oncogene experiments that report it do not have a public image and label set, and clinical imaging collections do not measure resting potential in that system. The result cannot be confirmed or refuted by analysis of data that are currently open.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In embryos expressing human oncogenes, compare the earliest membrane-voltage deviation with later tumor formation, against voltage-matched non-oncogene controls. Detection of a voltage anomaly before overt tumor, with usable sensitivity and specificity, would support the claim; voltage changes only after a tumor is visible, or no voltage change, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The voltage images and tumor scores are not publicly deposited.

Standard cancer imaging archives do not include embryonic membrane-voltage channels.

The result is from one experimental system without an open independent replicate.
